key_insight: An elastic vesicle containing extensile active particles can self-organize into distinct shape-and-flow states as activity increases, with membrane deformation and active nematic order strongly coupled.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests a route to tune soft micro-containers or synthetic cells by using boundary mechanics and anchoring interactions to control internal mixing, transport, and shape instability.
method: 2D weakly extensible elastic ring with bending rigidity in Stokes flow
Kinetic-theory model for a confined dilute active suspension
Hydrodynamic and energetic coupling via kinematic/dynamic boundary conditions and weak anchoring, validated with volume-conserving immersed-boundary simulations
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a closed-form quiescent equilibrium, a stability analysis predicting ordered activity thresholds, and nonlinear simulations that recover multiple emergent regimes including spindle, rotor, spinner, and turbulent states.
watch_item: The model is two-dimensional and relies on idealized weak anchoring and dilute-suspension assumptions, so quantitative transfer to real 3D vesicles may require careful calibration.
paper_title: Active Sculpting: morphodynamics of internally stirred active vesicles
